artists.biography:
Siouxsie and the Banshees were an English rock band formed in London in 1976 by vocalist Siouxsie Sioux and bass guitarist Steven Severin. Initially associated with the English punk rock scene, the band rapidly evolved to create "a form of post-punk discord full of daring rhythmic and sonic experimentation". The Times cited Siouxsie and the Banshees as "one of the most audacious and uncompromising musical adventurers of the post-punk era."
Their music combined elements of pop and avant-garde. The Banshees also became inspirational in the creation of the gothic rock genre. They disbanded in 1996, with Siouxsie and drummer Budgie continuing to record music as The Creatures, a second band they had formed in the early 1980s. In 2004, Siouxsie began a solo career.

perplexity.description:
The Scream is the debut studio album by Siouxsie and the Banshees, released in November 1978 on Polydor Records. Musically, the album stands apart from the straightforward punk rock of its era, embracing a more experimental and atmospheric approach. Characterized by jagged guitar lines, driving rhythms, and Siouxsie Sioux’s commanding vocals, the record blends elements of post-punk, art rock, and avant-garde sensibilities. Tracks like “Hong Kong Garden” and “Carcass” showcase the band’s ability to merge Eastern-inspired melodies with raw, visceral energy, while the overall sound is marked by its primal intensity and lack of conventional pop hooks.

As the band’s first full-length release, The Scream established Siouxsie and the Banshees as a major force in the post-punk movement. It marked the beginning of a long and influential career, setting the tone for their future explorations in mood and texture. The album was a commercial success, reaching No. 12 on the UK Albums Chart and earning a silver disc for sales. Critics at the time praised its originality, with many hailing it as one of the best debut albums of the year. Over time, The Scream has been recognized as a landmark release of the post-punk era, frequently cited alongside works by Public Image Ltd and Magazine for its lasting impact on alternative music.
